spec.title: About this view

options.content:
Is this host short of CPU, memory, disk or network, and which?

Missing or partial evidence is Unknown. [Runbook](https://github.com/iT3E/tnwks-ops/blob/main/docs/operations/grafana-resource-budget.md)

spec.description: Purpose, scope and the interpretation of missing evidence.

spec.title: CPU busy
spec.description:
Share of all logical processors doing work. Sustained above 80% leaves no room for a site failover.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Run queue per core
spec.description:
Threads ready to run but waiting for a processor, per core, over 5 minutes. Sustained above 2 the CPU is the bottleneck, whatever the busy figure says.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: WSL VM CPU busy

spec.expr: max by (k8s_cluster) (1 - avg by (k8s_cluster, instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on (k8s_cluster) max by (k8s_cluster) (windows_cpu_logical_processor{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"})

spec.description:
Share of the WSL VM's processors (its .wslconfig limit, fewer than the host's) doing work, from the cluster nodes on this host. Near 100% while the host still has room, the VM's limit is the ceiling.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: CPU by mode
spec.description:
Busy time split by mode. The WSL VM's work is counted as privileged time here (measured 2026-11-07: about 2.5 busy VM cores inside 3.5 privileged host cores), so privileged far above user is the cluster, not Windows apps.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Busiest cores
spec.description:
The five busiest logical processors. One core pinned near 100% while the total looks calm is a single-threaded bottleneck.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Run queue
spec.description:
Threads waiting for a processor, sampled. Short spikes are normal; a raised floor is saturation.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: WSL CPU pressure

spec.expr: max by (k8s_cluster) (rate(node_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (k8s_cluster) max by (k8s_cluster) (windows_cpu_logical_processor{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"})

spec.description:
Share of time at least one task in the WSL VM waited for a CPU (Linux PSI, read from the cluster nodes on this host). Rising pressure with a calm Windows CPU means WSL's processor limit, not the host, is the ceiling.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Memory in use
spec.description:
Physical memory not available to new work. Standby cache counts as available, so this is what the host can still give out.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Commit charge
spec.description:
Memory promised to processes against RAM plus page file. At 100% Windows refuses new allocations and programs fail, WSL's VM included, however much RAM looks free.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Paging to disk
spec.description:
Pages read from or written to the page file per second. A steady stream is memory saturation: work waits on the disk instead of RAM.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Memory and commit

spec.expr: max by (measure) (label_replace(1 - max by (instance) (windows_memory_available_bytes{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"}) / max by (instance) (windows_memory_physical_total_bytes{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"}), "measure", "In use", "", "") or label_replace(max by (instance) (windows_memory_committed_bytes{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"}) / max by (instance) (windows_memory_commit_limit{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"}), "measure", "Commit charge", "", ""))

spec.description:
Physical memory in use and commit charge over time. Commit climbing while use stays flat is memory reserved but untouched (WSL's VM reserves its whole limit).

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Page file traffic
spec.description:
Paging over time: line it up with slow disk or a busy CPU to see which came first.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: WSL memory pressure

spec.expr: max by (k8s_cluster) (rate(node_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (k8s_cluster) max by (k8s_cluster) (windows_cpu_logical_processor{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"})

spec.description:
Share of time at least one task in the WSL VM stalled reclaiming memory (Linux PSI). Above a few percent the VM's memory limit is too tight for its pods.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Slowest volume latency
spec.description:
Average time per disk operation on the worst volume. An SSD normally answers in under 5 ms; sustained above 20 ms the disk is what's slow.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Busiest volume
spec.description:
Share of time the busiest volume had work in flight. An SSD serves many requests at once, so read it with latency and queue: busy alone isn't saturation.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Queued disk requests
spec.description:
Requests waiting for the disk, averaged over 5 minutes. Sustained above 2 per disk, with latency rising, is disk saturation.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Read latency by volume
spec.description:
Average time per read. Spikes that line up with WSL I/O pressure are the slow disk the pods feel.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Write latency by volume
spec.description:
Average time per write. Cached writes are fast until the cache fills; a step up under load is the disk catching up.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Queue depth by volume
spec.description:
Requests waiting per volume, sampled.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Throughput by volume
spec.description:
Bytes read and written per second. High throughput with low latency is a busy, healthy disk.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: WSL I/O pressure

spec.expr: max by (k8s_cluster) (rate(node_pressure_io_stalled_seconds_total{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (k8s_cluster) max by (k8s_cluster) (windows_cpu_logical_processor{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"})

spec.description:
Share of time every runnable task in the WSL VM stalled on I/O at once (Linux PSI, full). This is how slow disk feels from inside the cluster: all nodes share one virtual disk on the host.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Free space by volume
spec.description:
Free share of each volume. Below 10% Windows and the VHDX that holds WSL's disk start to slow down; below 5% writes fail.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Busiest adapter

spec.expr: max by (instance) (sum by (instance, nic) (rate(windows_net_bytes_total{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])) / max by (instance, nic) (windows_net_current_bandwidth_bytes{k8s_cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$host"} > 0))

spec.description:
Traffic on the busiest adapter against its link speed. Near 100% the link is full; on Wi-Fi the link speed itself moves with the signal.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Received by adapter
spec.description:
Bytes received per second on each adapter in use.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Sent by adapter
spec.description:
Bytes sent per second on each adapter in use.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Errors and discards by adapter
spec.description:
Packets dropped or damaged per second. Errors are the link (cable, radio, driver); discards are a full buffer. None is the normal state.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.

spec.title: Link speed by adapter
spec.description:
Negotiated speed of each adapter with a link. A wired link that drops from 1 Gbit/s to 100 Mbit/s is a cable or port fault.

Observation budget: 180s for current evidence; backup/restore objectives and historical windows are separate. Source contract: observability/generated/panel-contracts.json.
